title: Lifting a resolution from modulo pi_i^8
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation, $A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal (the situation of [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]). Let $r\ge1$ and $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_r\in R$ with images in $\mathfrak q$. For an $R$-module $M$ and $x\in R$ write $\operatorname{Ann}_M(x)=\{m\in M:xm=0\}$. Assume (1) for $i=1,\dots,r$: $\operatorname{Ann}_{R/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^8)R}(\pi_i)=\operatorname{Ann}_{R/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^8)R}(\pi_i^2)$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_{\Lambda/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^8)\Lambda}(\pi_i)=\operatorname{Ann}_{\Lambda/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^8)\Lambda}(\pi_i^2)$; (2) for $i=1,\dots,r$ the image of $\pi_i$ in $A$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Put $\bar R=R/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)R$, $\bar A=A/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)A$, $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)\Lambda$ and $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)\Lambda$. If $\bar R\to\bar A\to\bar\Lambda\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution], then $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8 (lemma-lift-solution, line 2097), Section 07F6 (section-local), Situation Tag 07F7

proof.text: (The claim, by induction on $r$.) For $r\ge1$ let $P(r)$ be the assertion of the lemma for all data $(R,A,\Lambda,\mathfrak q,\pi_1,\dots,\pi_r)$ satisfying its hypotheses. We prove $P(1)$ (steps 3-6) and $P(r-1)\Rightarrow P(r)$ for $r\ge2$ (step 7); then $P(r)$ holds for all $r\ge1$. Throughout, $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}$ etc. are as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

proof.text: (Reduction modulo an ideal is again a situation of [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].) Let $J\subset R$ be an ideal with $J\Lambda\subset\mathfrak q$ (here $J=(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_s^8)R$, contained in $\mathfrak q$ after mapping since each $\pi_i\mapsto\mathfrak q$). Then $R/J$ is Noetherian, being an $R$-algebra of finite type ($n=0$) over the Noetherian ring $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; $A/JA\cong A\otimes_R R/J$ as $R/J$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], which is of finite presentation over $R/J$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]; $A\to\Lambda$ induces a homomorphism of $R/J$-algebras $A/JA\to\Lambda/J\Lambda$ (it maps $JA$ into $J\Lambda$); and $\mathfrak q/J\Lambda$ is a prime ideal of $\Lambda/J\Lambda$ since $J\Lambda\subset\mathfrak q$ and $(\Lambda/J\Lambda)/(\mathfrak q/J\Lambda)\cong\Lambda/\mathfrak q$ is a domain. Moreover for ideals $J\subset J'$ of $R$, the reduction of $R/J\to A/JA\to\Lambda/J\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q/J\Lambda$ modulo the image of $J'$ is canonically isomorphic to $R/J'\to A/J'A\to\Lambda/J'\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q/J'\Lambda$ (third isomorphism theorem $(M/JM)/(J'/J)(M/JM)\cong M/J'M$ for $M=R,A,\Lambda$, compatibly with all maps), and a resolution of one situation transported along an isomorphism of situations is a resolution of the other (the singular ideals, the ideals $\mathfrak h$ and the prime correspond).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F8 (lemma-lift-solution, lines 2097-2147)

proof.text: (Singular ideals map into singular ideals under base change; written out for the verification Stacks leaves implicit in the case $r=1$.) Let $R\to A$ be a ring map, $R\to R'$ a ring map and $A'=A\otimes_RR'$. Then the image of $H_{A/R}$ in $A'$ lies in $H_{A'/R'}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Indeed let $g\in A$ with $A_g$ smooth over $R$. Then $R'\to A_g\otimes_RR'$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1). Since $A\to A_g$ is a localization at $\{g^n\}$, the map $A'\to A'\otimes_AA_g$ is the localization of $A'$ at the powers of $g\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], and $A'\otimes_AA_g=(R'\otimes_RA)\otimes_AA_g\cong R'\otimes_RA_g$ as $R'$-algebras (associativity of the tensor product). Hence $A'_{g\otimes1}$ is smooth over $R'$, i.e. $g\otimes1$ lies in the set $G'$ of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] for $R'\to A'$. So the image of the ideal generated by $G$ lies in the ideal generated by $G'$, and if $h\in H_{A/R}=\sqrt{(G)}$, say $h^n\in(G)$, then $(h\otimes1)^n\in(G')$, so $h\otimes1\in\sqrt{(G')}=H_{A'/R'}$. We use it with $R'=R/\pi^8R$, $A'=A/\pi^8A$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]: the image of $H_{A/R}\Lambda$ in $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ lies in $H_{\bar A/\bar R}\cdot\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ (both maps to $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ are compatible), hence the image of $\mathfrak h_A$ lies in $\mathfrak h_{\bar A}$ (images of radical elements are radical over the image).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F8 (lemma-lift-solution, lines 2097-2147)

proof.text: (Case $r=1$: lifting the resolution.) Write $\pi=\pi_1$, $\bar R=R/\pi^8R$, $\bar A=A/\pi^8A$, $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$, $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/\pi^8\Lambda$. By hypothesis there is a resolution $\bar A\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda$ of $\bar R\to\bar A\to\bar\Lambda\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}$: $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $\bar R$ and $\mathfrak h_{\bar A}\subset\mathfrak h_{\bar C}\not\subset\bar{\mathfrak q}$. Hypothesis (1) for $i=1$ (the ideal $(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_0^8)$ is $0$) says $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$; hypothesis (2) for $i=1$ says $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$; $R$ is Noetherian and $A$ of finite presentation. So [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize-lifting-apply] (Stacks 07F0) applies to $A\to\Lambda$ and the factorization $\bar A\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda$ and gives a factorization $A\to B\to\Lambda$ with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$, $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ smooth, and $H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda\subset(\mathfrak h_B+\pi^8\Lambda)/\pi^8\Lambda$, where $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$. We show in steps 5-6 that $A\to B\to\Lambda$ is a resolution of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: ($\pi\in\mathfrak h_B$, hence $\pi^8\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$.) Let $g$ be the image of $\pi$ in $B$. The map $R\to R$ is smooth (polynomial ring in $0$ variables [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]), so $R\to R_\pi$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]; $B_\pi=B\otimes_RR_\pi$ is the localization $B_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], and $R_\pi\to B_g$ is smooth by step 4, so the composite $R\to R_\pi\to B_g$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2). Hence $g\in H_{B/R}$ by [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], so the image of $\pi$ in $\Lambda$ lies in $H_{B/R}\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$, and $\pi^8\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$. Consequently $(\mathfrak h_B+\pi^8\Lambda)/\pi^8\Lambda=\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$, a radical ideal of $\bar\Lambda$ (its preimage $\mathfrak h_B$ is radical), and step 4 gives $H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$, hence $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}=\sqrt{H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda}\subset\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$: every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ whose class lies in $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}$ lies in $\mathfrak h_B$.

proof.text: (Case $r\ge2$, assuming $P(r-1)$.) Put $R'=R/\pi_1^8R$, $A'=A/\pi_1^8A$, $\Lambda'=\Lambda/\pi_1^8\Lambda$, $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q/\pi_1^8\Lambda$, a situation as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] by step 2, and let $\pi'_1,\dots,\pi'_{r-1}\in R'$ be the images of $\pi_2,\dots,\pi_r$; they map into $\mathfrak q'$. Hypothesis (1) for $(R',\Lambda',\pi'_j)$, $j=1,\dots,r-1$: $R'/(\pi_1'^8,\dots,\pi_{j-1}'^8)R'=R/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_j^8)R$ and $\Lambda'/(\pi_1'^8,\dots,\pi_{j-1}'^8)\Lambda'=\Lambda/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_j^8)\Lambda$ (step 2), on which $\pi'_j$ acts as $\pi_{j+1}$, so this is hypothesis (1) of the lemma for $i=j+1$. Hypothesis (2): $\pi_{j+1}$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$, so its image $\pi_{j+1}\otimes1$ is strictly standard in $A\otimes_RR'\cong A'$ over $R'$ [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-base-change] [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (Stacks: 'property (2) is preserved by Lemma 07CC'). By step 2 the reduction of $R'\to A'\to\Lambda'\supset\mathfrak q'$ modulo $(\pi_1'^8,\dots,\pi_{r-1}'^8)$ is isomorphic to $R/(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)R\to A/(\dots)A\to\Lambda/(\dots)\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q/(\dots)\Lambda$, which can be resolved by assumption. By $P(r-1)$, $R'\to A'\to\Lambda'\supset\mathfrak q'$ can be resolved, i.e. the reduction of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ modulo $\pi_1^8$ can be resolved. Finally $P(1)$ applied to $(R,A,\Lambda,\mathfrak q,\pi_1)$, whose hypotheses are (1) and (2) for $i=1$, shows that $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved. This proves $P(r)$.
